items.headline: Rays’ losing streak at Globe Life Field reaches 10 games
items.text: Tampa Bay fell 6-0 to Texas, extending its losing streak at Globe Life Field to 10 games while remaining in a tight AL playoff race.
items.freshnessBasis: Texas defeated Tampa Bay 6-0 on September 3, extending the Rays’ venue losing streak to 10 games.

items.headline: Adley Rutschman homers twice in memorable return to Baltimore
items.text: Rutschman celebrated his return to Camden Yards with two home runs as Boston defeated Baltimore, 6-5.
items.freshnessBasis: Rutschman returned to Baltimore’s Camden Yards and hit two home runs in Boston’s September 3 win.

items.headline: Cubs trim Brewers with 2-1 win in NL Central matchup
items.text: Chicago defeated Milwaukee, 2-1, behind Kevin Gausman’s nine strikeouts and Pete Crow-Armstrong’s 39th home run. Milwaukee remains atop the NL Central, but the loss denied the Brewers another divisional win.
items.freshnessBasis: Chicago beat Milwaukee 2-1 on September 3 in a game with direct NL Central and postseason implications.

items.headline: Pirates win fifth series in six tries
items.text: Pittsburgh defeated San Francisco, 5-2, for its fifth series victory in the club’s last six series, continuing a late-season surge.
items.freshnessBasis: Pittsburgh beat San Francisco 5-2 on September 3 and MLB reported the Pirates’ fifth series win in their last six.

items.headline: Dodgers walk off Cardinals, 3-2
items.text: Teoscar Hernández delivered a walk-off hit as Los Angeles defeated St. Louis, 3-2, keeping the Dodgers in the crowded NL postseason race.
items.freshnessBasis: Los Angeles defeated St. Louis 3-2 on a walk-off September 3.

items.headline: Astros beat White Sox, 6-2, in AL Central race
items.text: Houston defeated Chicago, 6-2, behind a four-run third inning and a home run from José Altuve. The White Sox remain atop the AL Central despite the loss.
items.freshnessBasis: Houston defeated Chicago 6-2 on September 3 as both clubs continued competing in the AL postseason picture.

items.headline: Blue Jays defeat Guardians, 6-3
items.text: Toronto beat Cleveland, 6-3, behind a strong offensive performance from Nathan Lukes and Brett Bateman.
items.freshnessBasis: Toronto defeated Cleveland 6-3 on September 3.

items.headline: 49ers arrive in Melbourne ahead of historic Week 1 matchup with Rams
items.text: San Francisco’s traveling party landed in Melbourne after a 15-hour charter flight and will spend the week acclimating before facing the Los Angeles Rams in the NFL’s Australia opener.
items.freshnessBasis: NFL.com reported the 49ers’ arrival in Melbourne on September 4, beginning their week-long preparation for the September 11 season opener.

items.headline: Ben Simmons agrees to one-year deal with Kings, returning to NBA
items.text: Ben Simmons agreed to a one-year, $3.5 million contract with Sacramento after sitting out the entire 2025-26 season. The former No. 1 pick is expected to provide veteran depth behind rookie point guard Darius Acuff Jr.
items.freshnessBasis: Simmons’ agreement with Sacramento was reported on September 4.

items.headline: Amen Thompson signs five-year, $208M extension with Rockets
items.text: Houston signed Amen Thompson to a five-year, $208 million rookie-scale extension, securing a key piece of its young core through the 2030-31 season.
items.freshnessBasis: The Rockets made the extension official on September 3.

items.headline: Timberwolves officially sign Jonathan Kuminga
items.text: Minnesota announced the signing of forward Jonathan Kuminga. Terms were not disclosed; Kuminga joins the Timberwolves after splitting the 2025-26 season between Atlanta and Golden State.
items.freshnessBasis: Minnesota announced Kuminga’s signing on September 4.

items.headline: Stars sign Jack Williams as emergency goalie replacement
items.text: Dallas signed Jack Williams as an emergency goalie replacement, according to the league transaction log.
items.freshnessBasis: The transaction was listed for Friday, September 4, 2026, within the 24-hour window.

items.headline: Liverpool agree January move for Saint-Etienne forward Djylian N'Guessan
items.text: Liverpool have agreed a deal to sign 18-year-old French forward Djylian N'Guessan from Saint-Etienne. He will remain in France on loan with Stade Brestois before joining Liverpool permanently in January.
items.freshnessBasis: Liverpool officially announced the agreement on September 4, 2026.

items.headline: Barcola cleared to be available for Liverpool debut at Ipswich
items.text: Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola said new signing Bradley Barcola will be available for the trip to Ipswich, subject to completing Thursday training. A start is considered unlikely because he lacks preseason match minutes.
items.freshnessBasis: Liverpool's manager provided a new availability update ahead of Friday's Premier League match.

items.headline: Newcastle remain without four injured players for Bournemouth visit
items.text: Newcastle are expected to be without Dan Burn, Joelinton, Tino Livramento and William Osula against Bournemouth. Manager Matthias Jaissle also declined to comment on reports that Osula could face a long-term absence.
items.freshnessBasis: Newcastle's manager and team-news reporting provided updated injury and availability information on September 4.

items.headline: Colorado Rapids land Morgan Whittaker in club-record deal
items.text: Colorado acquired the 25-year-old winger from Middlesbrough for a reported club-record $10.7 million fee. Whittaker signed through the 2029-30 MLS season with an option for 2030-31 and will occupy a Designated Player slot.
items.freshnessBasis: Colorado announced the signing on Friday, September 4.

items.headline: NYCFC face major availability issues ahead of Nashville match
items.text: New York City FC listed Drew Baiera, Arnau Farnós, Talles Magno, Maxi Moralez, Keaton Parks, Kai Trewin and Hannes Wolf out with leg injuries. Nashville listed Warren Madrigal out with a lower-body injury.
items.freshnessBasis: MLS published the Matchday 24 player status report on Friday, September 4.

items.headline: Three players suspended for Matchday 24
items.text: Colorado's Hamzat Ojediran and Real Salt Lake's Morgan Guilavogui are suspended for yellow-card accumulation. San Diego FC's Jeppe Tverskov is suspended after receiving a second caution and red card.
items.freshnessBasis: The MLS disciplinary summary was current as of September 3 and carried into the Matchday 24 slate.

items.headline: NYCFC host Nashville with both clubs entering Matchday 24
items.text: New York City FC are scheduled to host Nashville SC at Yankee Stadium on Friday, September 4. The matchup became ticker-worthy after MLS released the same-day player status report detailing extensive NYCFC absences and Nashville's Warren Madrigal injury.
items.freshnessBasis: The September 4 player status report materially changed the availability picture for the scheduled match.

items.headline: Toronto add Bulgarian midfielder Alejandro Piedrahita on loan
items.text: Toronto FC added midfielder Alejandro Piedrahita on loan from CSKA Sofia, according to the league's updated transfer tracker.
items.freshnessBasis: The MLS transfer tracker was updated through September 4 with the loan move.

items.headline: Real Salt Lake loan Victor Olatunji to SK Beveren
items.text: Real Salt Lake moved forward Victor Olatunji to Belgian club SK Beveren on loan, according to the updated MLS transfer tracker.
items.freshnessBasis: The transaction appeared in MLS's transfer tracker updated through September 4.

items.headline: Toronto transfer Deandre Kerr to AVS Futebol SAD
items.text: Toronto FC transferred forward Deandre Kerr to Portugal's AVS Futebol SAD, according to MLS's updated transaction tracker.
items.freshnessBasis: The transaction appeared in MLS's transfer tracker updated through September 4.

items.headline: Federal court hears SEC effort to block former pros from LSU roster
items.text: A federal court in Alabama heard the SEC’s attempt to prevent LSU from using former professional players, escalating the eligibility dispute after a Louisiana judge issued an injunction favoring the athletes.
items.freshnessBasis: AP newly reported the federal hearing on September 4, 2026, within the 24-hour window.

items.headline: Colorado rallies past Georgia Tech 14-13 on late TD and blocked field goal
items.text: Colorado overcame a 13-7 deficit with 42 seconds remaining, then blocked Georgia Tech’s potential winning field goal as time expired in the season opener.
items.freshnessBasis: The season-opening result was newly reported on September 4, 2026.

items.headline: Minnesota’s Javon Tracy sets program record with two punt-return touchdowns
items.text: Javon Tracy returned two punts for touchdowns in Minnesota’s 59-7 season-opening win over Eastern Illinois, establishing a single-game school record.
items.freshnessBasis: AP newly reported the record-setting performance on September 4, 2026.

items.headline: UMass ends 16-game losing streak with 37-21 win over Rutgers
items.text: UMass snapped a 16-game losing streak as Pop Watson III threw three touchdown passes in the season opener for both teams.
items.freshnessBasis: AP newly reported the streak-ending result on September 4, 2026.

items.headline: No. 21 Utah routs Idaho 66-14 in Morgan Scalley’s regular-season debut
items.text: Utah opened the season with a 52-point victory behind three touchdown passes from Devon Dampier and three touchdowns from Wayshawn Parker.
items.freshnessBasis: AP newly reported the completed season opener on September 4, 2026.

items.headline: No. 25 Missouri defeats Arkansas-Pine Bluff 54-14 in opener
items.text: Austin Simmons threw four touchdown passes in his Missouri debut as the Tigers opened the season with a 40-point win.
items.freshnessBasis: AP newly reported the completed season opener on September 4, 2026.

items.headline: Illinois beats UAB 42-23 behind Katin Houser’s four total touchdowns
items.text: Katin Houser threw three touchdown passes and ran for another as Illinois defeated UAB in the season opener.
items.freshnessBasis: AP newly reported the completed season opener on September 4, 2026.

items.headline: Kennesaw State shuts out West Georgia 47-0 in season opener
items.text: Rickie Collins accounted for three touchdowns and Latrelle Murrell scored twice as Kennesaw State opened the season with a dominant shutout.
items.freshnessBasis: AP newly reported the completed season opener on September 4, 2026.

items.headline: Delaware opens season with 42-7 win over Merrimack
items.text: Nick Minicucci passed for 330 yards and two touchdowns and added a rushing score in Delaware’s emphatic season-opening victory.
items.freshnessBasis: AP newly reported the completed season opener on September 4, 2026.

items.headline: Zverev survives another five-set marathon to reach US Open third round
items.text: Top seed Alexander Zverev defeated Quentin Halys 6-4, 4-6, 7-6(3), 6-7(3), 6-3 in a four-hour, 33-minute second-round match.
items.freshnessBasis: The official US Open reported the result early Friday, September 4, after Thursday night's match.

items.headline: Australia beats Puerto Rico 70-54 in opening-day action
items.text: Australia controlled its World Cup opener against Puerto Rico, winning 70-54 in Berlin.
items.freshnessBasis: FIBA reported the completed opening-day game on September 4.

items.headline: Russell tops FP2 as Leclerc splits Mercedes at Monza
items.text: George Russell led second practice in 1:22.559, 0.120 seconds ahead of Charles Leclerc, with Kimi Antonelli third and Lando Norris fourth.
items.freshnessBasis: Formula 1 published the FP2 results at 15:19 UTC on Friday, September 4.

items.headline: Leclerc leads Ferrari 1-2 in FP1
items.text: Charles Leclerc set the pace in first practice ahead of Ferrari teammate Lewis Hamilton, with George Russell third.
items.freshnessBasis: Formula 1 published the FP1 report at 11:46 UTC on Friday, September 4.

items.headline: Albon hit with 20-place penalty and will start from the back
items.text: Alexander Albon received a cumulative 20-place grid penalty for power-unit changes, meaning he will start at the back of the Italian Grand Prix grid.
items.freshnessBasis: Formula 1 announced the penalty Friday afternoon during the Monza race weekend.

items.headline: Antonelli faces a notional 30-place grid drop at home race
items.text: Kimi Antonelli's engine-related penalties will force him to start from the back unless further penalties alter the order; he is set to share the back row with Albon.
items.freshnessBasis: Formula 1 reiterated the penalty situation in Friday's post-practice coverage.

items.headline: Norris says McLaren is not in pole-position fight after practice
items.text: Lando Norris finished fourth in FP2 but said McLaren was not currently in the fight for pole after trailing Russell by 0.384 seconds.
items.freshnessBasis: Norris's assessment was published after Friday's two practice sessions at Monza.
